rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge primarily concerns resurrection and a new creation after death, but is phrased broadly to cover creation in general: are humans or the encompassing heaven harder to create?
rows.anchor: Burada asıl mâna ölümden sonra yeni bir hilkatle yaratılış üzerindedir. Fakat bir kübrâ hâlinda daha şümullü olmak üzere sual mutlak halk üzerinde îrâd olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven is the more immense creation: humans are like a particle within it, yet God built it by joining diverse subtle and dense materials and celestial bodies into an ordered whole through various forces.
rows.anchor: بَنَىٰهَا} o Allah onu binâ etti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Building means joining separate components to one another so their combination forms a whole; heaven is such a constructed whole.
rows.anchor: “Binâ” müteferrik eczâyı yekdiğerine zamm u rabt ile mecmû‘undan bir kül inşâ etmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised heaven to a great height without pillars.
rows.anchor: boyuna irtifâ‘verdi direksiz olarak yükseğe[^1] kaldırdı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Semk is a thing’s height or vertical extension from bottom upward; considered from above downward it is called umq. Some also explain it as thickness in breadth and length.
rows.anchor: “Semk” bir şeyin “irtifâ‘” tâbir ettiğimiz boyu, aşağıdan yukarıya imtidâdı ve yüksekliğidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven was balanced, ordered, and set right, as in the verse saying God raised heaven and established the balance.
rows.anchor: mîzânını vaz‘edip denkleştirdi, nizâmına koyup düzeltti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the inference that this wording proves the entire heaven has a perfect spherical form; that overall shape is not established, and its detail is known to God.
rows.anchor: bütün semânın hey’et-i umûmiyesinin şekli tam küre olduğu sâbit değildir. Tafsîlini Allah bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss derives the verb from darkness and renders it as making the night dark; this attribution is only incidental to some contents of heaven, since not all of heaven is night.
rows.anchor: “gatş”tan olduğuna göre gecesini karanlık etti, muzlim kıldı diye mâna verilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Kāmûs
rows.claim: Kāmûs records gatsh and gatashān as slow walking caused by illness or old age; from this Elmalılı derives the sense of making the night go gradually.
rows.anchor: “gatş” ve “gataşân” Kāmûs’ta mezkur olduğu üzere hastalıktan veya ihtiyarlıktan nâşî âheste âheste yürümek mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers understanding the phrase as gradually moving the night away, which fits the bringing forth of daylight better than simply darkening it.
rows.anchor: “gecesini tedrîcen giderdi” demek olur. Bu ise şu ihrac ile pek mütenâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duha originally means the spreading of the sun’s light and the duration of daytime, later naming the familiar morning hours; here, as the opposite of night, it means light or daytime generally.
rows.anchor: “duhâ” fi’l-asl ziyâ-yı Şems’in inbisâtı ve gündüzün imtidâdı demek olup sonra mâruf kuşluk vaktine isim olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows two readings: the daily alternation of night and day relative to Earth, involving Earth’s creation and the Moon’s extinction, or night gradually disappearing from heaven itself.
rows.anchor: Ve bunda iki mâna mümkindir. Birisi evvelki gibi Arz’a nazaran olan ve her gün te‘âkub eden gecesi gündüzü olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He favors night and daylight as states of heaven itself because these words are directly attributed to heaven. Darkness is privative: before the sun and other lights existed heaven was dark; as they were created, night receded, though shadows from Earth and other bodies remain locally.
rows.anchor: buradaki geceyi ve gündüzü -dediğimiz gibi- semânın kendisinin gecesi ve gündüzü diye anlamak bize daha muvâfık görünüyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After heaven was created and ordered and its night removed and daylight brought forth, God spread Earth so its surface could support life and habitation, laying out its crust as a bed.
rows.anchor: yeryüzünü üzerinde hayat ve süknâ kābil olacak vechile yayıp serdi, Arz’ın üzerinde yaşadığımız kışrını ondan sonra yaratıp döşek hâlinde döşedi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dahw or dahy means spreading; bast is to spread or lay something out as one spreads a bed.
rows.anchor: “Dehâ” bast etmek mânasına “dahv” veya “dahy”dendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sequence is that Earth itself had already been created before its later spreading and preparation for habitation.
rows.anchor: Bunun zâhiri de Arz’ın kendisinin daha evvel yaratılmış olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although 2:29 and 41:10–12 may seem to put heaven’s ordering after Earth and its contents, Elmalılı takes thumma there as rhetorical precedence in rank, not temporal delay; ba‘da dhālik here clarifies the sequence.
rows.anchor: orada ثُمَّ zamanda terâhî için değil, kelâmda terâhî-i rütbî için olmak lâzım geleceğini buradaki بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ îzah ediyor demektir.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Moon shone like the Sun before it was effaced; on this account early Earth had no night darkness before the Moon went dark.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan vârid olan rivayette Kamer, mahvedilmezden evvel Güneş gibi parlak olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that report, darkening the night refers to the Moon’s extinction creating night on Earth; ba‘da dhālik suggests this happened before Earth’s spreading, though the Moon’s formation after Earth implies a later adjustment to heaven after Earth’s creation.
rows.anchor: وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا Kamer’in sönmesiyle Arz üzerinde gecenin karartılmış olmasını ifade etmiş ve Kamer’in sönmesi de Arz’ın dahvinden evvel olduğunu da بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ karînesiyle anlatmış olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought forth Earth’s water by creating it, gushing its springs and flowing its rivers, and made its grasses, pastures, and cultivated growth appear.
rows.anchor: suyunu yarattı, menbalarını fışkırttı, nehirlerini akıttı, otunu, otlağını mezrasını bitirdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set Earth’s mountains firmly in place.
rows.anchor: Dağlarını da oturttu tesbit etti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth’s spreading makes its crust fit for life and habitation, providing benefit and sustenance for people and animals; this great act is purposeful rather than futile or accidental, and life has wisdom and an end.
rows.anchor: bu büyük sun‘u kudret hikmetsiz değil, bunlar gayesiz abes olarak, keyfemettefak yaratılıvermemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭāmma al-kubrā is one of the names of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: “tâmme-i kübrâ”, kıyametin isimlerindendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the sense illustrated by 21:24, Qur’an is named al-Dhikr; 15:9 and 3:58 are cited as Qur’anic uses of that name.
rows.anchor: İşte bu mâna ile Kur’ân’ın bir ismi de “ez-Zikr”dir: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is also called al-Ḥukm; Elmalılı says the meaning of that name was discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: “Hükm” isminin mânası da geçmişti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is also called rūḥ, since it is the spirit of a great spiritual life; 42:52 is cited for this name, and these names are all found in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’a “rûh” da denilmiştir. Çünkü büyük bir hayât-ı ma‘- neviyenin rûhudur.

rows.speaker: Üseyd b. Hudayr
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Bukhari reports that while Usayd b. Hudayr recited Sūrat al-Baqara, angels descended successively in the darkness to the sound of his recitation.
rows.anchor: Buhârî’de de Üseyd b. Hudayr radıyallahu ‘anh Hazretleri’nin[^3] Sûre-i Bakara okumasıyla sesine karanlıkta peyderpey melâike inmiş olduğu

rows.speaker: Ukbe b. Âmir
rows.claim: Ukba ibn Amir reports that at the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet exhorted them to hold fast to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Ukbe[^6] b. Âmir radıyallahu ‘anh demiştir ki: “Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Haccetü’l-vedâ‘da bize[^7] ahd verdi de buyurdu ki: (عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْقُرْآنِ)

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: Asked which reciter was best in recitation or voice, the Prophet said it was the one whose fear of God is evident when heard.
rows.anchor: Bir de Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports clarify that reading Qur’an and tafsir aims at reminding those who fear God: the Qur’an was not sent to impose hardship, but as a reminder for the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: Bununla Kur’an ve tefsir okumaktan maksad ne olduğunu da anlamış oluyoruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prays that God illuminate their hearts with the light of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Heman Cenâb-ı Allah kalblerimizi nûr-i Kur’an ile tenvîr buyursun.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is called al-Hudā because it is described as guidance for people and for believers.
rows.anchor: olduğu için bir de “el-Hüdâ” tesmiye edilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because it illuminates hearts and thoughts, the Qur’an is also named al-Nūr; 7:157 is cited.
rows.anchor: kalbleri, fikirleri tenvîr etmesi itibariyle bir ismi de “en-Nûr”dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr is a verbal noun meaning remembering or remembrance, and can also mean the thing remembered.
rows.anchor: “Zikr” dahi esasen masdar olup anmak, anış ve anılan şey mânalarını dahi ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering may take place in the heart or on the tongue.
rows.anchor: Anmak da ya kalb veya lisan ile olur.

rows.speaker: Râgıb ve Kāmûs sâhibi
rows.claim: Raghib in al-Mufradat and the author of al-Qamus in Basa’ir describe dhikr as the inner state by which a person preserves acquired knowledge.
rows.anchor: Râgıb’ın[^6] Müfredât’ta[^7] ve Kāmûs sâhibinin[^8] Besâir’de beyan ettikleri üzere “zikr” maddesiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that sense dhikr is synonymous with hifz, but hifz secures something in the heart whereas dhikr recalls it into awareness.
rows.anchor: Lâkin hıfz kalbde ihrâzı ve zikri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can also mean a thing’s being present to the heart or to speech.
rows.anchor: Bazen de zikr bir şeyin kalbe veyahut

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is heart remembrance and tongue remembrance; each can be recalling after forgetting or continuing to remember without ever forgetting.
rows.anchor: Biri “kalben zikr”, biri de “lisânen zikr”dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr also means name and fame, praise and commendation, and honor or status; it is used for prayer and supplication.
rows.anchor: Sonra zikir, nâm ve şöhret, medh u senâ, şeref ü şân mânalarına gelir. Namaza ve duâya ıtlak edilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can refer to heavenly books that set out religion and law and establish the community’s rulings; 54:25 and 21:105 illustrate this sense.
rows.anchor: Bir de zikr, din ve şerî‘atı tafsîl ve ahkâm-ı milleti vaz‘eden semâvî kitaplara denir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an uses āya in each of the previously discussed senses, all of which are gradations of the notion of an evident sign.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da “âyet” kelimesi yerine göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its most specific legal-religious usage, an āya is a Qur’anic section separated by a pause marker and forming a complete unit in the Qur’an’s arrangement.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın harflerinden bir fâsıla ile ayrılmış olan zümrelerinden her birine bir âyet denilir ki bunlar Kur’ân’ın nazmında birer cüz’-i tâm teşkîl ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most verses are independent statements of one or several sentences, but some are only a distinct single or compound qualifier; al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm in al-Fātiḥa are one verse comprising two attributes, not a sentence.
rows.anchor: Âyetlerin ekserîsi bir veya birkaç cümleden müteşekkil müstakil birer kelâmdırlar. Ma‘amâfîh içlerinde bir cümle teşkil etmeyen müfred veya mürekkeb mümtaz birer sıfat gibi kayıt hâlinde bulunanlar da vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudhāmmatān is a single word, yet it can be recited independently with the force of a complete utterance and paused upon.
rows.anchor: bir kelimedir, böyle iken bunlar bir kelâm neş’esiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Muddaththir, thumma naẓara is two words forming one sentence, while thumma ʿabasa wa-basara is four words forming two sentences.
rows.anchor: Müddessir sûresinde ثُمَّ نَظَرَ [el-Müddessir 74/21][^6] iki kelime bir cümledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses have short, medium, and long forms; examples range from about half a page for Āyat al-Kursī and the ablution verse to a full page for Āyat al-Mudāyana.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle âyetlerin kısası, ortası, uzunu ve her birinin mütenevvi‘mertebeleri vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse-final letters (fawāṣil) are not always uniform; they vary through patterns that may or may not be specific.
rows.anchor: Fâsıla harfleri de dâima muttarid değil, gâh mahsus, gâh gayr-i mahsus farklarla tenevvü‘eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because verse forms and endings vary, the separation and ordering of verses are tawqīfī: they depend on transmitted reports and cannot be determined by reason alone as poetic lines or sajʿ units can.
rows.anchor: âyetlerin ayrılması ve tertîbi tevkīfîdir. Yani şiirin mısrâ‘ı, seci‘in fıkrası gibi yalnız dirayet ile tâyin olunamaz, rivayete mütevakkıf olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason alone cannot establish that Ḥā-Mīm and ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf comprise two verses; their verse division is known through transmission.
rows.anchor: حٰمٓ. عٓسٓقٓ iki âyet olduğu yalnız dirayet ile bilinemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By extension, any Qur’anic section that expresses a divine ruling is also called an āya.
rows.anchor: Daha sonra Kur’ân’ın ahkâm-ı ilâhiyeden bir hüküm ifade eden her kısmına da bir âyet ıtlak
